title: Exception
description: The canonical Exception object. Source: Aether_Workforce_OS_Full_Build.pdf Section 5.1 ('Exception object (canonical)') and Aether_Ambition_Build_Plan.pdf Stage II. Every field here has a same-named column in 03-Product-OS/data/reference-data-model/schema.sql's `exception` table — the two must be changed together.

source_id.description: Identifier of the upstream record that triggered this exception (e.g. a time_punch id or a pay_run_line_item id). Lets a human trace the exception back to raw data.

earning_type.description: The earning_code.code this exception concerns, e.g. 'OT' or 'REG'.

current_value.description: The value as it currently stands in the draft pay run (e.g. hours or dollars).

baseline_value.description: The expected value given the employee's own history and/or the crew's history.

baseline_window.description: What baseline_value was computed over, e.g. '12_week_trailing_average'. Must always be stated in plain terms — this is what makes explanation_plain checkable by a human.

suggested_value.description: The copilot's proposed correction. Omitted when the recommended action is 'flag only, no numeric correction available'.

dollar_impact_employer.description: Signed dollar impact to the employer if suggested_value is approved instead of current_value.

dollar_impact_employee.description: Signed dollar impact to the employee's net pay if suggested_value is approved instead of current_value.

explanation_plain.description: Plain-language explanation with numbers and denominators. Per the Operating Plan's voice-of-product rule: never 'leverage', never a bare confidence percentage on a money movement.

confidence_internal.description: INTERNAL PRECISION TRACKING ONLY. Never surfaced in any UI or customer-facing API response — used only to compute the true-positive / false-positive rates referenced in Operating Plan 5.1. A response serializer that includes this field outside an internal analytics context is a bug.

recommended_action.description: What the operator console should ask a human to do, e.g. 'Approve a correction to 8.0 hours regular, or keep as-is and note the reason.'

approver_id.description: Set once a human has acted on this exception. Null while decision is 'pending'.

reason_code.description: Required whenever decision is 'rejected' or 'noted_no_change' — the human's stated reason, from a controlled vocabulary maintained per legal_entity.

audit_hash.description: Hash of (source_id + policy_version + model_version + output), per Operating Plan Section 7: 'every agent action that touches pay is audited: input snapshot, policy version, output, approver.'

timestamp.description: When this exception was generated, not when it was decided (see decided_at in the data model for that).

examples.explanation_plain: Maria's overtime is 42% above her 12-week baseline. The Saturday shift looks like a clock-out miss against the posted schedule.
examples.recommended_action: Approve a correction to 8.0 hours regular, or keep as-is and note the reason.
